{{short description|Espionage jargon}}
{{use mdy dates|date=July 2021}}
A '''limited hangout''' or '''partial hangout''' is a tactic used in [[media relations]], [[perception management]], [[politics]], and [[information management]]. The tactic originated as a technique in the [[espionage]] trade.

== Concept ==
According to [[Victor Marchetti]], a former special assistant to the [[Deputy Director of the Central Intelligence Agency|deputy director]] of the [[Central Intelligence Agency]] (CIA), a limited hangout is "spy jargon for a favorite and frequently used gimmick of the clandestine professionals. When their veil of secrecy is shredded and they can no longer rely on a phony cover story to misinform the public, they resort to admitting—sometimes even volunteering—some of the truth while still managing to withhold the key and damaging facts in the case. The public, however, is usually so intrigued by the new information that it never thinks to pursue the matter further".<ref>{{cite news|last=Marchetti|first=Victor|author-link=Victor Marchetti|date=August 14, 1978 |title=CIA to 'Admit' Hunt Involvement in Kennedy Slaying|url=https://www.cia.gov/readingroom/docs/CIA-RDP81M00980R000600230023-6.pdf|newspaper=[[The Spotlight]]|pages=4–6|access-date=2023-02-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210918200332/https://www.cia.gov/readingroom/docs/CIA-RDP81M00980R000600230023-6.pdf|archive-date=2021-09-18|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=1983-11-28 |title=720 F2d 631 Hunt v. Liberty Lobby Dc |volume=F2d |issue=720 |page=631 |url=http://openjurist.org/720/f2d/631 |publisher=OpenJurist |access-date=2016-07-13}}</ref> While used by the CIA and other intelligence organizations, the tactic has become popularized in the corporate and political spheres.<ref>{{cite web |date=12 July 2022|title=Escaping the limited hangout |url=https://globalintelhub.com/escaping-the-limited-hangout/ |website=Global Intel Hub |access-date=20 July 2022}}</ref>

== Modified limited hangout ==<!--'Modified limited hangout' redirects here-->
In a March 22, 1973, meeting between United States President [[Richard Nixon]], [[John Dean]], [[John Ehrlichman]], [[John N. Mitchell]], and [[H. R. Haldeman]], Ehrlichman incorporated the term into a new and related one, "'''modified limited hangout'''".<ref>{{cite AV media|people=[[David Frost|Frost, David]]; Nixon, Richard |year=1977|title=[[Nixon interviews|Frost/Nixon: The Complete Interviews]]|publisher=Paradine Television}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|last=Safire|first=William|author-link=William Safire|date=26 March 1989|title=On Language; In Nine Little Words|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1989/03/26/magazine/on-language-in-nine-little-words.html|magazine=[[The New York Times Magazine]]|access-date=23 June 2013}}</ref>

The phrase was coined in the following exchange:<ref name="Transcript">{{cite web|title=Transcript of a recording of a meeting among the President, John Dean, John Ehrlichman, H.R. Haldeman, and John Mitchell on March 22, 1973 from 1:57 to 3:43 p.m.|url=http://www.hpol.org/transcript.php?id=130|publisher=History and Politics Out Loud|access-date=2006-08-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040104040234/http://www.hpol.org/transcript.php?id=130|archive-date=2004-01-04|url-status=dead}}</ref>

{{Pull quote|PRESIDENT: You think, you think we want to, want to go this route now? And the{{snd}}let it hang out, so to speak?<br />
DEAN: Well, it's, it isn't really that –<br />
HALDEMAN: It's a limited hang out.<br />
DEAN: It's a limited hang out.<br />
EHRLICHMAN: It's a modified limited hang out.<br />
PRESIDENT: Well, it's only the questions of the thing hanging out publicly or privately.}}

Before this exchange, the discussion captures Nixon outlining to Dean the content of a report that Dean would create, laying out a misleading view of the role of the White House staff in events surrounding the [[Watergate scandal|Watergate burglary]]. In Ehrlichman's words: "And the report says, 'Nobody was involved{{'"}}. The document would then be shared with the [[United States Senate Watergate Committee]] investigating the affair. The report would serve the administration's goals by protecting the President, providing documentary support for his false statements should information come to light that contradicted his stated position. Further, the group discusses having information on the report leaked by those on the Committee sympathetic to the President, to put exculpatory information into the public sphere.<ref name="Transcript" />

The phrase has been cited as a summation of the strategy of mixing partial admissions with [[misinformation]] and resistance to further investigation, and is used in political commentary to accuse people or groups of following a Nixon-like strategy.<ref>{{cite news|last=Carroll|first=Jon|author-link=Jon Carroll|date=2002-05-01|title=The Richard Nixon playbook|url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?file=/chronicle/archive/2002/05/01/DD150649.DTL|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020606025830/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?file=/chronicle/archive/2002/05/01/DD150649.DTL|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 6, 2002|newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|access-date=2006-08-27}}</ref> It has also been described as the release of a package of sensitive information mixed with discoverable falsehoods in hopes that discovery of the falsity of part will lead to the entire package being considered false,<ref name="Wexler Hancock 2018 p. 201">{{cite book |last1=Wexler |first1=Stuart |last2=Hancock |first2=Larry |year=2018 |title=Killing King: Racial Terrorists, James Earl Ray, and the Plot to Assassinate Martin Luther King Jr. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=n-AREAAAQBAJ |publisher=Catapult |page=[https://books.google.com/books?id=n-AREAAAQBAJ&pg=PT201 201]|isbn=978-1-64009-022-4|access-date=2022-04-10}}</ref> and as the release of a package with a core of falsehoods wrapped in secret but verifiable information in hopes that verification of the wrapping will reinforce the believability of the false core.<ref>{{cite book|last=Ebrahim|first=Zahir|year=2012|title=The Poor-Man's Guide to Modernity|url=http://lust-for-life.org/Lust-For-Life/_Textual/ZahirEbrahim_ThePoorMansGuideToModernity_2011_336pp/ZahirEbrahim_ThePoorMansGuideToModernity_2011_336pp.pdf|edition=3rd|publisher=Project Humanbeingsfirst|page=20}}</ref>

Writing in ''[[The Washington Post]]'', [[Mary McGrory]] described a statement by [[Pope John Paul II]] regarding [[Catholic Church sexual abuse cases|sexual abuse by priests]] as a "modified, limited hangout".<ref>{{cite news |last=McGrory|first=Mary |author-link=Mary McGrory|date=2002-04-25|title=From Rome, A 'Limited Hangout' |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A44668-2002Apr24.html |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |page=A29|access-date=2010-04-30}}</ref>
